title: Guru Succession and Nadir's Question About the Sikhs

blocks.text: A listener asks for an account of the line of Gurus after Guru Nanak, and the reply moves briskly through the succession from Guru Angad onward. The summary highlights the transmission of spiritual authority, the miri-piri ideal, martyrdom, and the culmination of sovereignty in the Guru's final shaping of the Khalsa.

This condensed rehearsal of Sikh history is not ornamental. It explains why the Panth acts with such independence: its political courage is presented as the outcome of a sacred lineage rather than a sudden rebellion.

By the end of the page the narrative pivots back to imperial bewilderment. Nadir Khan asks who these raiders are, so the historical survey becomes the setup for the coming description of Sikh character and warfare.
